newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-MUSTER'S DREAM MELTS AWAY IN ROMAN HEAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MUSTER'S DREAM MELTS AWAY IN ROMAN HEAT.

text.p: Defending champion Thomas Muster saw his dream of a third successive Italian Open title die in the heat of a gruelling three-hour battle with unseeded Australian Scott Draper at the Foro Italico on Wednesday.

The third seed, unbeaten in Rome since the third round in 1994 and three times a winner, received treatment for dehydration after losing his second round match 7-6 5-7 7-5 in temperatures of 32 degrees Celsius.
Muster's exit leaves the tournament without four of its top five seeds after two rounds for the first time.
Reigning Wimbledon champion and fifth seed Richard Krajicek joined the list of big-name casualties when he surrendered in straight sets to German Marc-Kevin Goellner.
The Dutchman, a finalist here last year, lost 7-6 7-6 after losing the two tie-breaks 8-6 and 7-1.
The world's top two players Pete Sampras and Michael Chang lost in the first round on Tuesday.
Draper, who eliminated Hamburg Open winner Andrei Medvedev in the first round but had never previously beaten a top 10 player, defeated Muster at his own game.
"He's probably recognised as one of the toughest players on clay in the world and the scary part about it is that I actually won physically and mentally," said the world number 75.
While the centre court furnace dehydrated a man famed for his fitness, Draper -- familiar with the heat and humidity of his hometown Brisbane in Queensland -- revelled in it.
"I love the heat because I know I can handle it better than most other players," he said.
At times, the Australian even outdid the Austrian's tough guy image, continually shouting at himself and hurling his racket to the ground in anger at unforced errors.
Most significantly, it was Draper and not Muster who dictated the match and gradually ground down his opponent. "I tried to impose my game on him and it worked," he said.
Muster had started strongly, leading 4-2 with a break in the first set but Draper broke back to 4-4. Muster promptly broke him again but failed to serve out the set.
In the tiebreak, Draper rushed into a 3-0 lead and never relinquished his lead, taking it 7-4 with strong serves and a series of breathtaking backhand winners down the line.
Draper broke to lead 2-0 in the second before the heat started to get to him as well. "I had a letdown," he said, "the first set was the toughest I've ever played.
In a topsy-turvy set, both men held breakpoints until Muster levelled the match on his second set point.
The final set saw both men squander chances to break but it was clear that Muster was starting to struggle while Draper continued to chase down every ball.
At 5-5, the Austrian finally ceded his serve on a double fault and Draper needed no second invitation to close out the match on the second of three matchpoints.
Asked to account for successive wins over two of the clay court games finest exponents, Draper replied:
"It's funny what a week can do. If you'd seen me this time last week, you'd have thought, God, who's this guy."
Defeat means Muster has now failed to progress beyond the third round at any of his four tournaments on clay this season.
Jim Courier, who claimed world number one Sampras's scalp in the first round, reached the third round for the first time for three years with a straight sets win over Spanish qualifier Albert Portas.
Courier, unseeded despite having won this tournament twice in 1992 and 1993, won a first set tiebreak 7-5 before racing away with the second 6-2.
But Tuesday's other giantkiller Hernan Gumy, who knocked out Chang, was brought back to earth by another unseeded former champion Sergi Bruguera of Spain 6-1 6-4.
